gloss: to enjoy (as a pastime); to have refined taste in; to be well-mannered

definitions.gloss: to enjoy (as a pastime); to have refined taste in; to dabble in
definitions.explanation: To enjoy or practice something as a hobby or cultivated pursuit, often implying modest skill. Frequently used when humbly describing one's own hobbies.

definitions.gloss: to be well-mannered; to exercise self-restraint; to be proper
definitions.explanation: To behave in a restrained, dignified, and socially appropriate manner. This sense often appears in the form たしなみ (noun).

examples.japanese: {若|わか}い{頃|ころ}、{茶道|さどう}を{少|すこ}したしなんでいた。
examples.english: When I was young, I dabbled a little in tea ceremony.

examples.japanese: {父|ちち}は{囲碁|いご}をたしなむ{人|ひと}で、{週末|しゅうまつ}はいつも{碁|ご}を{打|う}っている。
examples.english: My father is someone who enjoys go, and he always plays on weekends.

examples.japanese: {身|み}だしなみに{気|き}をつける。
examples.english: To pay attention to one's grooming.

examples.japanese: {社会人|しゃかいじん}としてのたしなみを{持|も}つ。
examples.english: To have the proper decorum expected of a working adult.

examples.japanese: {大人|おとな}のたしなみとして、{最低限|さいていげん}のマナーは{身|み}につけておきたい。
examples.english: As a matter of adult decorum, I want to have at least basic manners.

notes:
An elegant, somewhat literary verb with two related but distinct senses. In sense 1, it conveys modest enjoyment of a cultivated pursuit — using たしなむ to describe one's hobbies is more humble than saying {趣味|しゅみ} (hobby). In sense 2, it relates to propriety and self-discipline.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {酒|さけ}をたしなむ: to drink (moderately/with refinement)
- {茶道|さどう}をたしなむ: to practice tea ceremony (as a hobby)
- {俳句|はいく}をたしなむ: to enjoy composing haiku
- {身|み}だしなみ: personal grooming/appearance
- {大人|おとな}のたしなみ: adult decorum/refinement

KANJI:
Can be written as {嗜|たしな}む, but the kanji is uncommon and hiragana is more typical.

REGISTER:
Slightly literary and refined. Using this verb to describe one's hobbies implies modesty and cultivation.
